title: CSP-44: sample index four-ninths and time index five-ninths with linear quantum workspace

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), the single CSP-44 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise m the least integer with m^9>=n^4, kappa=ceil(log2 m)+1, dl=ceil((n+1+m*kappa-m*(m-1)/2)/(m+1)), H=dl+m-1, widths lambda_i=dl+i and root width1, u=ceil(log2 n), Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), exact high-part storage, counted radix/query joins, capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch total charged work is O(n^(31/9)log2(n)2^F(n)), F(n)=n^(5/9)+(1/2)n^(4/9)-n^(1/9), with stronger main-branch bound O(n^3 log2(n)2^(m+dl)). Every source, failed attempt, scan lookup, radix bit, address, initialization and reset is included. Its exact growth index is5/9, jointly with the other claims. For n=1 logarithmic resource envelopes use their positive values at n=2; this finite extension does not change any structured asymptotic form.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), the single CSP-44 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise m the least integer with m^9>=n^4, kappa=ceil(log2 m)+1, dl=ceil((n+1+m*kappa-m*(m-1)/2)/(m+1)), H=dl+m-1, widths lambda_i=dl+i and root width1, u=ceil(log2 n), Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), exact high-part storage, counted radix/query joins, capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch peak classical workspace is O(n2^F(n)) bits, F(n)=n^(5/9)+(1/2)n^(4/9)-n^(1/9), with stronger main-branch bound O(H2^H) using exact common-prefix/high-part tables, all radix/rank arrays, siblings, scratch and decoder records. Its exact growth index is5/9, jointly with the other claims. For n=1 logarithmic resource envelopes use their positive values at n=2; this finite extension does not change any structured asymptotic form.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), the single CSP-44 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise m the least integer with m^9>=n^4, kappa=ceil(log2 m)+1, dl=ceil((n+1+m*kappa-m*(m-1)/2)/(m+1)), H=dl+m-1, widths lambda_i=dl+i and root width1, u=ceil(log2 n), Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), exact high-part storage, counted radix/query joins, capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch peak accessible quantum workspace is O(n) qubits, including the depth-first stack, physical source/data, extractor, modular and lookup scratch, root bank and reset wires. Its exact growth index is0, jointly with the other claims; no QRAM or coherent bank is used. For n=1 logarithmic resource envelopes use their positive values at n=2; this finite extension does not change any structured asymptotic form.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), the single CSP-44 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise m the least integer with m^9>=n^4, kappa=ceil(log2 m)+1, dl=ceil((n+1+m*kappa-m*(m-1)/2)/(m+1)), H=dl+m-1, widths lambda_i=dl+i and root width1, u=ceil(log2 n), Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), exact high-part storage, counted radix/query joins, capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch total acquired copies, including rejected labels and aborted work, are O(n^(14/9)log2(n)2^(n^(4/9))). On the main branch only, Q<=(Y+6)Ccap+2nCp+Kp with Ccap=32dl2^m(Kc+u+16), Cp=32dl2^m(Kp+u+16), Y=ceil(log2 Ccap); finite exhaustive recovery uses at most N(n+10) copies, included through uniform asymptotic constants. The exact sample growth index is4/9, jointly with the other claims. For n=1 logarithmic resource envelopes use their positive values at n=2; this finite extension does not change any structured asymptotic form.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), the single CSP-44 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise m the least integer with m^9>=n^4, kappa=ceil(log2 m)+1, dl=ceil((n+1+m*kappa-m*(m-1)/2)/(m+1)), H=dl+m-1, widths lambda_i=dl+i and root width1, u=ceil(log2 n), Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), exact high-part storage, counted radix/query joins, capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. The proved malformed fraction is epsilon(n)=0 under independent ideal copies. No positive robustness or its impossibility is claimed. All four resource bounds hold jointly under this promise. For n=1 logarithmic resource envelopes use their positive values at n=2; this finite extension does not change any structured asymptotic form.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
